newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ parliament committee ends Peters deliberations.
newsitem.headline: NZ parliament committee ends Peters deliberations.

text.p: The New Zealand Parliament's powerful privileges committee on Wednesday ended deliberations over a contempt allegation against Deputy Prime Minister and Treasurer Winston Peters, but remained tight-lipped on his fate.
Committee chairman and Attorney-General Paul East indicated after the meeting that the panel had reached a decision, but said its report could not be released until the House sits again on April 22.
"I am hopeful we will not be required to meet again on the matter and will be able to report to parliament when parliament resumes," he said.
The contempt of parliament allegation against Peters was made by left-wing Alliance leader Jim Anderton after a fracas between Peters and government backbencher John Banks on March 5.
Banks and Anderton said in evidence Peters had assaulted and threatened Banks outside the debating chamber after a close division over legislation to delay tax cuts.
Peters said he only put a hand on Banks to indicate he wanted to continue talking.
The eight-member committee is equally divided between the government and opposition parties.
Parliamentary sources said the matter could yet go to the full parliament for debate.
"The government (MPs) are solidly behind Peters," one opposition MP said.
Peters is the leader of nationalist New Zealand First, the junior partner in New Zealand's coalition government.
